SMTO-GWT-0061 — SMTO couldn't confirm it was still the same GPU

GUID: 28015c25-a755-579d-8562-70613181d244
Slug: gpu-device-identity-changed
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gpu

What happened

  • SMTO stopped because it couldn't be sure the GPU it was working on stayed the same throughout, for example because GPU numbers changed. For a settings change, SMTO stopped before making it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to list the GPUs on this Gateway. GPU numbers can shift after a restart or driver change, so you need the current list.
  2. Repeat your request and name the GPU by its ID (UUID) from that list, not just its number. SMTO only changes GPU settings when it can tie the request to one exact GPU.
  3. If this happened while SMTO was taking repeated GPU readings, start the readings again once every GPU appears in the list. A GPU disappeared during the readings, so SMTO stopped instead of switching to another GPU.

What success looks like

  • Your request finishes and reports the same GPU ID you asked for.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway computer. GPUs that keep appearing and disappearing can point to a hardware or driver problem there.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A GPU identity check failed: expected UUID mismatch, an index-based change without expected_uuid, a changed index after admission, an ambiguous XML match, or a selected device missing during sampling.

What this means

  • GPU identity checks found a mismatched expected UUID, an index mutation without expected_uuid, a changed index after admission, an ambiguous XML match or a selected device missing during sampling. The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.

Why this can happen

  • GPU identity checks found a mismatched expected UUID, an index mutation without expected_uuid, a changed index after admission, an ambiguous XML match or a selected device missing during sampling.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare expected UUID, current discovery and retained sample or admission state; distinguish a missing identity guard from actual device change.

How to fix it

  • Run gpu.devices again and resubmit with the exact UUID; index-based configuration requests must include expected_uuid matching that index. For sampling failures, partial samples are in the receipt details; restart sampling with explicit UUIDs and check nvidia-smi -L for GPUs that dropped off or were reordered.
  • Discover devices again and submit the exact UUID; index mutations require expected_uuid.

Retry and execution caution

  • Discover devices again and submit the exact UUID; index mutations require expected_uuid.

How to verify the fix

  • The exact intended UUID resolves and any index-based mutation includes its matching expected UUID.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, kill GPU clients automatically or invent sensor values.

Technical notes

  • The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
